claims: Yellow fever is not commonly found in the United States.
Typhoid is not commonly found in the United States.
Japanese encephalitis is not commonly found in the United States.
Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended for most travelers to countries where the disease is common.
Typhoid vaccine is recommended for travelers visiting smaller cities, villages, and rural areas, particularly in South Asia.
Yellow fever vaccine is required for entry into certain countries in Africa and South America.
Yellow fever vaccination often requires an International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP).
Japanese encephalitis vaccine is recommended for travelers planning a month or longer in endemic areas in Asia.
Japanese encephalitis vaccine is recommended for short-term travelers visiting rural areas.
Rabies vaccine is recommended for travelers going to remote areas.
Rabies vaccine is recommended for animal handlers.
Rabies vaccine is recommended for those staying for long periods in countries where rabies is common.
Meningococcal disease vaccine is required for travelers going to Saudi Arabia for Hajj/Umrah.
Meningococcal disease vaccine is recommended for the "meningitis belt" of Africa.
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) vaccine is recommended for travelers to endemic areas in Europe and Asia who will be hiking, camping, or spending time outdoors.
A polio booster is currently recommended for adults traveling to over 30 countries with recent poliovirus detections.
A stamped ICVP is valid 10 days after the yellow fever vaccine is administered.
